about.text:
Ki-Lo delete account: deleting your account from inside the app (KEY-1117, design brief KEY-1120). Mobile only. Each board shows one phone at 390 x 844 twice, dark on the left and light on the right. Draft for Zee's review.

Rulings drawn (Zee, 24 November 2026):
• Deletion is immediate and permanent. There is no grace period.
• An email account re-enters its password on the confirm step, once forgot password (KEY-1111) has landed. A Google account gets the confirmation only. Until KEY-1111 lands every account gets the confirmation only.

The flow: More, Account, Delete account opens the Delete account screen. Delete account on that screen opens the confirm. Delete account in the confirm deletes. Success signs the person out and lands on Sign in with a confirmation. A failure closes the confirm and shows on the Delete account screen. If the connection drops before the answer comes back, the unconfirmed board shows there instead.

Kit parts used as they ship: ListRow with titleTone danger, SheetHeader stack, Card, Banner (review, offline, error, success), Button (destructive, secondary, primary), ConfirmDialog with tone destructive, Input, and the Sign in screen from the canvas Ki-Lo password reset and change. A dashed outline marks what is new on More.

Sample data (invented): the account is sam.taylor@example.com, as on the password canvas. The contact address is the one the Terms give, COMPANY_DETAILS.contactEmail in packages/core/src/copy/legal.ts.

n-row1-copy.text:
Row 1 · every string and accessible name

tab-shell.more · delete-account-row
• Header: More
• Settings rows in view are the shipped ones, unchanged.

• Row: Export my data, subtitle A file with everything in your account. Name: Export my data, A file with everything in your account.

• Header title: Delete account. Back button name: Back to More.
• Card heading: What Ki-Lo deletes
• List: Your diary / Your own foods and recipes / Your weight and body measurements / Your programme and targets / Your training / Your assistant conversations / Your achievements / What Ki-Lo keeps on this phone
• Card caption: Error reports and what the assistant sent to Anthropic can stay with those services for up to 30 days.
• Warning banner (a note, not an alert): Your account is deleted at once. This cannot be undone.
• Row: Export my data, subtitle Save a copy first. Name: Export my data, Save a copy first.
• Buttons: Delete account, Keep my account. Each is named by its words.

delete-account · explain-offline

• Delete account is disabled and says so to a screen reader. Every other string is as on explain.

n-row1-behaviour.text:
Row 1 · behaviour

• The Delete account row is the last row in Account, after Sign out. Only its title takes the danger tone (ListRow titleTone danger). The icon tile stays neutral. It has a chevron because it opens a screen. It shows for every signed-in account.
• When Change password (KEY-1111) lands it sits between Export my data and Sign out. Delete account stays last.
• The row opens Delete account as a stack screen over the tabs, as Export my data does. Opening it deletes nothing.
• Back, Keep my account and the Android back button all return to More.
• Export my data opens the existing Export my data screen. Back from there returns to Delete account.
• The Delete account button opens the confirm (row 2). It never deletes by itself.
• The list names areas, not tables. What Ki-Lo keeps on this phone is the offline copy the Privacy Policy describes and the settings kept on the device. The app clears both when the deletion succeeds.
• The caption under the list is there because the Privacy Policy says Sentry's error reports and Anthropic's copies can outlast a deleted account by up to 30 days. The screen should not promise more than the policy does.
• Offline: the quiet offline banner sits above the card and Delete account is disabled at 40 per cent, because the deletion runs on the server. Back, Keep my account and Export my data stay as they are. When the connection returns the banner goes and the button works, with no reload.
• The screen scrolls when the text is larger than drawn. The two buttons stay fixed at the bottom.

choices.text:
Choices for Zee (drawn as recommended)

1. The row sits last in the Account group, after Sign out. Alternative: above Sign out.
2. The confirm is the existing destructive dialog with two buttons and no typed word. Alternative: type a word to confirm.
3. The explain list is by area, eight lines, not one line per table.
4. Sign in confirms with a success Banner, not a Toast. A toast closes itself after 5 seconds and can be missed. The banner stays until the person moves on.
5. The explain card carries one caption about the two 30-day exceptions in the Privacy Policy (Sentry, Anthropic). Alternative: leave it to the policy.
6. While deleting, the dialog's title and body change to Deleting your account and This can take a moment. Keep Ki-Lo open. Alternative: keep the question and show only the spinner.
7. A failure closes the dialog and shows as an error banner on the Delete account screen. Try again opens the confirm again. Alternative: show the error inside the dialog.
8. Forgot password? in the confirm closes it and opens Reset your password with the account's email filled in.
9. The password is checked when Delete account is pressed, as on Sign in. The button is not held disabled while the field is empty.
10. Sign in keeps its heading, Welcome back, after a deletion. Alternative: Sign in as the heading on this one arrival.
11. Keep my account says my, as Export my data does on the approved export boards, although the design system prefers your for the person's things. Alternative: Keep account.
12. On the explain screen Delete account is the filled destructive button, because it is the point of the screen. In the dialog it is the secondary button with danger words, as ConfirmDialog draws a destructive answer.
13. When the answer never comes back (delete-account · unconfirmed), a warning Banner says Ki-Lo could not confirm the deletion, Try again repeats the request with no second confirm, and the other button says Back to More, because Keep my account may not be true there. Alternative: keep the label Keep my account.

Row 2 · every string and accessible name

delete-account · confirm
• Title: Delete your account?
• Body: Everything in your account is deleted now. This cannot be undone.
• Buttons: Delete account (danger words on the secondary button), Keep my account (the primary button).
• The dialog is an alert dialog named by its title. A screen reader starts on the title.

delete-account · confirm-password
• Title: Delete your account?
• Body: Everything in your account is deleted now. This cannot be undone. Enter your password to confirm.
• Field label and name: Password
• Link: Forgot password?
• Buttons: Delete account, Keep my account.

delete-account · confirm-password-wrong
• Field error (an alert): That password is not right. Nothing was deleted.
• Every other string is as on confirm-password.
• Not drawn, existing sentences on the same field: Enter your password (the field was empty) and Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

delete-account · deleting
• Title: Deleting your account
• Body: This can take a moment. Keep Ki-Lo open.
• Delete account shows the button spinner in place of its words. Spinner name: Deleting your account.
• Keep my account is disabled and says so to a screen reader.

n-row2-behaviour.text:
Row 2 · behaviour

• The confirm is the shipped ConfirmDialog with tone destructive, as Delete all conversations uses it: a card centred over the dim, Delete account as the secondary button with danger words, Keep my account as the primary button, so the way back is the easy one.
• Which confirm: a Google account always gets delete-account · confirm. An email account gets confirm-password once KEY-1111 has landed. Until then every account gets confirm.
• Delete account starts the deletion. Keep my account, a press on the dim, the screen reader's escape gesture and the Android back button all close the dialog and delete nothing. The Delete account screen is still underneath.
• confirm-password: the field is not focused when the dialog opens, so the question is read first. When the keyboard opens, the card moves up to stay clear of it. The password is checked when Delete account is pressed, as on Sign in. The dialog needs a slot for the field, which ConfirmDialog does not have today.
• Forgot password? closes the dialog and opens Reset your password (KEY-1111) with the account's email filled in. Nothing is deleted.
• Wrong password: the dialog stays open, the field takes the danger border and shows the error, the typed password stays, and nothing is deleted. Editing the field clears the error.
• Deleting: the title and body change, Delete account shows the spinner and ignores presses, and Keep my account is disabled. The step cannot be dismissed: the dim, the escape gesture and the Android back button do nothing until the attempt ends. The password field, when there is one, is locked. ConfirmDialog today blocks only its confirm button while busy, so it needs a way to refuse dismissal.
• Success: the person is signed out, what Ki-Lo keeps on this phone is cleared, and Sign in opens with the confirmation (row 3).
• Failure: the dialog closes and delete-account · failed shows (row 3).

n-row3-behaviour.text:
Row 3 · behaviour

delete-account · failed
• This board shows only when the server answered that nothing was deleted. That is why it can say Nothing was removed: the account and everything in it are as they were. A connection that drops before the answer comes back is delete-account · unconfirmed instead.
• The banner is announced when it appears. It stays until the next attempt or until the person leaves the screen.
• Try again opens the confirm again, with an empty password field for an email account. It does not delete by itself.
• Email hello@sojisoft.com opens the phone's mail app with the address filled in. The address is COMPANY_DETAILS.contactEmail, the one the Terms give for deleting an account.
• Back, Keep my account and the Android back button return to More.
• If the phone is also offline, the offline banner shows under the error banner and Try again is disabled until the connection returns.

sign-in · account-deleted
• Recommended: a success Banner, not a Toast. A toast closes itself after 5 seconds and sits under the status bar, so someone who looks away can miss the only confirmation that a permanent action went through. The banner sits in the reading order above the form and stays until the person signs in, opens Create account or leaves the screen.
• The banner is a status. It is announced once and focus is not moved to it. It does not show again the next time Ki-Lo opens.
• The fields start empty. The deleted account's email is not filled in.
• The Android back button leaves Ki-Lo. There is no way back into the deleted account.
• Forgot password? under the Password field is KEY-1111's, drawn so the two canvases agree. Until it lands the screen has no such link.
• Nothing else on Sign in changes, the heading included.

n-row3-unconfirmed.text:
delete-account · unconfirmed · behaviour, and why it is drawn this way

• When it shows: the request was sent and the connection dropped before the answer came back, so Ki-Lo cannot tell whether the account was deleted. The dialog closes and this board shows. Nothing on the phone is cleared and the person is not signed out.
• Why the warning Banner (the review variant) and not the error red: red says a thing failed, and here nothing is known to have failed. The account may well be gone. Warning is the kit's tone for something that needs the person's attention. The quiet offline banner was the other candidate. It is not used because a quiet banner is never announced, and this is a result the person is waiting on, so the banner is raised as an alert (the Banner's announce option, which only the review variant has).
• The banner says what is known (the deletion could not be confirmed), what may be true (the account may already be deleted) and what to do. It never says Nothing was removed.
• Try again sends the request again at once, with no confirm and no password, because the person has already confirmed and a second attempt is always safe: it either deletes the account or finds it already gone. While it runs the button shows its spinner (named Deleting your account), Back to More is disabled and the screen cannot be left, as on delete-account · deleting. That busy state is not drawn.
• After Try again: deleted, or already gone, opens Sign in with Your account has been deleted. An answer that nothing was deleted shows delete-account · failed. No answer again keeps this board.
• The second button says Back to More, not Keep my account. Keep my account would be a promise Ki-Lo cannot make here, since the account may already be gone. Back to More is the header button's own name and does the same thing. Alternative: keep the label Keep my account so the footer reads the same in every state.
• Back to More, the header's Back and the Android back button return to More and send nothing. Recommended: if the account is in fact gone, the next time Ki-Lo reaches the server it signs the person out and opens Sign in with the same confirmation.
• No email action. Trying again settles it either way. The email route stays on delete-account · failed, where the server has answered.
• While the phone is offline, Try again is disabled at 40 per cent and works again when the connection returns. The offline banner is not added, because this banner already says to check the connection.
• The card, the banner about permanence and Export my data stay, so the screen reads as it did before the attempt.
